verdict: consistent once the opening group is read: 32 signs = 32 letters, 7 groups = 7 words (5,4,6,4,6,4,3), one letter per shape (23/23 repeated); the cipher has a five-sign word يخوتا before شحطت (probably يا اخوتا, "O my brothers", written as one word: the "word of two words in Mushaf spelling" beginning with يا of the solving story), and دياركم as one group; tentative
notes: Rows 3-5 of image 0084_0128 (15 + 13 + 4 = 32, as the record). Plain 1.4x zooms of each half line, 2-3x on the first group. The last four groups give the key with no conflict (فعسى تخصونا بطيف كرى, 17 signs); with it the second group is شحطت (Ad Rk Kk Et: K = ط as in بطيف, the 2-headed sweep = ت as in تخصونا) and the third is دياركم (< = ي, S-hook = ا, circle-dot = ر, U-loop = ك as in كرى). The first group, 5 signs, is < Kc Vb Et Ak = ي خ و ت ا with that key (Kc, the kaf-hook joined to a cup, is the خ of تخصونا; Vb the و of تخصونا). The written plaintext on 62v l.8 does not have this word; the story (the master said one word was "a word of two words written in the Mushaf spelling, like يا ايها"; the compiler guessed "its beginning is يا") fits يا اخوتا contracted to يخوتا, as يا ايها is written يايها / يأيها. This reading of the first word is the key's, not checked against any written text: tentative. If Kc were two signs (S-hook = ا + a cup) the group would be يا?وتا (6 signs); the hook and the cup touch in both places, so it is counted once.
